Your only responsibility is to give intelligent and creative feedback and constructive criticism to variables, given an objective specified in <OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> </OBJECTIVE_FUNCTION> tags. Pay attention to the role description of the variable, and the context in which it is used. You should assume that the variable will be used in a similar context in the future. Only provide strategies, explanations, and methods to change in the variable. DO NOT propose a new version of the variable, that will be the job of the optimizer. # - <VARIABLE>: Specifies the span of the variable.

payload.instruction: Change the background into a basketball court
payload.rubric: Judge requested image editing: yes means all requested changes are complete, no means no requested change has progressed, partial means some progress without complete fulfillment. Unrelated edits are not requested progress. Insufficient evidence stays unresolved.

node.question: Is there visible evidence that the background has begun changing toward a basketball court, even though the requested court background is not complete?
node.criteria: Pass if the image shows a discernible but incomplete change of the background toward a basketball court. Fail if there is no visible progress toward that change. Unknown if progress cannot be distinguished from the original or assessed reliably.
node.binding: Assess progress only toward replacing the background with a basketball court; unrelated edits do not count.

node_traces.evidence: The kitchen background has been replaced with a basketball setting, including a hoop, court floor markings, and basketballs. This is clear progress toward the requested background change.

fulfillment: The node’s criteria and trace conflict: s1 says the image lacks court markings, but the edited image visibly has a light playing surface and curved court lines; s2 also describes court-floor markings while the aggregate remains partial. Reconcile the dependency evidence against the actual image and make the completion decision depend on whether the background as a whole reads as a basketball court, not on an unsupported claim that markings are absent. The dark, featureless upper backdrop may still make the setting ambiguous, so assess that visual evidence explicitly rather than treating basketball props or the background replacement alone as proof of completion. Preserve the distinction between complete fulfillment, partial progress, and unresolved evidence; do not force the reference label.

response.content: {"text":"The node’s progress-only wording appears to cap the result at partial even when the requested edit is complete. Reconcile the parent and downstream evidence with the edited image; do not treat a conflicting claim that markings are absent as fact. Keep partial for genuinely incomplete edits and unknown for unreliable evidence, rather than forcing the reference label. No transport or schema failure is indicated."}
